items.prompt: Which sentence starts the right way?
hints: Look at the first letter of each sentence.
A sentence starts with a capital letter.
Find the sentence that starts with a big letter.
items.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter. My starts with a capital M.

options.why: A sentence starts with a capital letter.
Only the first letter should be a capital.

items.prompt: What goes at the end of this sentence? 'I like rice'
hints: Is the sentence asking something?
It is a telling sentence.
Telling sentences end with a little dot.
items.explanation: I like rice tells us something. A telling sentence ends with a full stop.

options.why: A comma goes inside a sentence.
This sentence does not ask anything.

items.prompt: Write the name with a capital letter: dewi
hints: Names always start with a capital letter.
Only the first letter changes.
Write a big D, then the rest of the name.
items.explanation: Dewi is a name. Names start with a capital letter.

items.prompt: Which word should always start with a capital letter?
hints: Names of people always have a capital letter.
Look for a name.
Which word is a girl's name?
items.explanation: Rani is a name, so it always starts with a capital letter: Rani.

options.why: Cat only needs a capital at the start of a sentence.
Red only needs a capital at the start of a sentence.

items.prompt: Which word should have a capital letter? 'Yesterday i went to the park.'
hints: Check the start of the sentence first.
When you write about yourself, one little word is always a capital.
Look for a word with only one letter.
items.explanation: When I means me, it is always a capital letter: I went to the park.

options.why: Yesterday is at the start and already has a capital.
Park is not a name.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The first word has a capital letter.
The last word has a full stop.
Start with the capital letter. What comes next?
items.explanation: The bird can sing. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

items.prompt: Choose 2 sentences that are written correctly.
hints: Check the start of each sentence.
Check the end of each sentence.
A correct sentence has a capital letter and a full stop.
items.explanation: We like the beach. and I can swim. both start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.

options.why: The first word needs a capital T.
This needs a full stop at the end.

items.prompt: Write this sentence with a capital letter at the start. 'my bag is red.'
hints: Look at the first word.
Only the first letter needs to change.
Write a big M to start.
items.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter: My bag is red.

items.prompt: Where should the full stop go? 'I have a cat It is black.'
hints: There are two ideas here.
Find where the first idea ends.
The second sentence starts with a capital letter.
items.explanation: The first sentence is 'I have a cat.' The second sentence starts with It.

options.why: I have. is not a whole idea.
It needs to start the next sentence.

hints: Names start with a capital letter.
The word I is always a capital.
Find the sentence with both capitals.
items.explanation: Ali is a name and I is always a capital. Only Ali and I play. has both capitals.

options.why: Sam is a name and I is always a capital.
I is always a capital letter.
Mia is a name, so it needs a capital.

items.prompt: How many sentences are here? 'The sun is up. Birds sing. I wake up.'
hints: Each sentence ends with a full stop.
Count the full stops.
Point to each full stop and count.
items.explanation: There are 3 full stops, so there are 3 sentences.

options.why: Count the full stops again.
There are 9 words. Count the full stops instead.

items.prompt: Which words always need a capital letter? Sort them.
hints: Names of people and places always have a capital.
Other words only need a capital at the start of a sentence.
Start with budi. Is it a name?
items.explanation: Budi and Sari are names of people. London is the name of a place. They always need a capital letter.

items.prompt: How many capital letters are missing? 'my friend tom and i like to swim.'
hints: Check the start of the sentence.
Look for a name.
Remember the word I.
items.explanation: My needs a capital, Tom is a name and I is always a capital. That is 3.

options.why: Look at the start, at the name and at the word i.
Look again at the little word i.
Friend and swim do not need capitals.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: Start with the word that has a capital letter.
End with the word that has a full stop.
Who is the sentence about? Then say what it can do.
items.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop: The dog can run.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The first word has a capital letter.
The last word has a full stop.
Say who is speaking, then what they like.
items.explanation: The sentence is I like red apples. It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
